nom: PanOxyl Acne Creamy Wash with 4% Benzoyl Peroxide

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily skin report it becomes less oily and more controlled with regular use, and several use the product specifically to reduce shine without complaint of over-drying.
segments.dry: Reviewers who describe their skin as dry generally say the wash does not strip or tighten their skin the way other benzoyl peroxide products have, though a few still note dryness with frequent use.
segments.combination: The one reviewer specifying combination, breakout-prone skin reports redness and a hot sensation right after application, suspecting an allergic reaction to the benzoyl peroxide.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin most often say this 4% version is gentler than the 10% version and does not burn, strip or irritate them, though one reviewer with sensitive combination skin reports a reaction and one other reviewer describes an itchy red rash and increased bumpiness after use.
segments.mature: One reviewer in her 40s dealing with hormonal acne reports the wash cleared her skin with zero inflammation.

concerns.aging: Not enough reviewers discuss visible aging specifically; the few mentions of dark spots relate to acne marks rather than wrinkles or firmness.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers say the wash cleans without stripping, tightness or peeling, and several highlight it as surprisingly non-drying for a benzoyl peroxide product; a smaller group states it does dry their skin, especially with daily use, and recommends pairing with a moisturizer or reducing frequency.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers report reduced redness and a calmer complexion over time, including for razor burn and ingrown hairs; against this, one reviewer describes a persistent hot, red reaction after each use and another describes an itchy red rash spreading across the face.
concerns.barrier: Reviewers generally feel the product cleanses without compromising the skin barrier or leaving it feeling stripped; one reviewer with dry, sensitive, eczema-prone skin says it is the only cleanser that hasn't triggered a flare-up, while one reviewer reports mold-like specks in the cap of her tube, unrelated to formula tolerance.
concerns.spots: Reviewers frequently report fewer new breakouts, faster healing of active spots, and cleared cystic or hormonal spots within one to three weeks; a couple of reviewers say they still saw some acne spots or purging despite continued use.
concerns.blemishes: Many reviewers describe clearer, smoother skin and fading blemishes with regular use, including on the back, chest and underarms; a few note lingering acne marks even as active breakouts improve.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily skin report the wash reduces shine and helps control oil production without over-drying, with no dissent noted on this point.

aspects.libelle: Does not strip or over-dry skin
Can dry out skin with frequent use

Similarly to another review under thus product, I tried this once and not too long after an itchy, red rash appeared on both sides of my jawline and eventually moved to other parts of my face. Before I tried this product, I had smooth and mostly clear skin with some small breakouts sometimes appearing around my chin, lips, nose and forehead. Now, my skin is so bumpy around my forehead and cheeks. Be cautious.

I have combination skin prone to breakouts. I have used PanOxyl products before, but this time I decided to try their gel. After applying it , I massage my skin for 1-2 min, immediately afterwards, my face turns red and feels hot - a reaction to the benzoyl peroxide. I used it once a day and followed up with moisturizer, leaving my skin feeling soft. However, the redness persists , so I seem to be allergic to it. In the photo, it might look like there's no change, but in person , my pores have tightened slightly, and any pimples that do appear are less noticeable and clear up quickly.

I really enjoyed trying out this face wash. I have used a 10% wash before, and that one really dried and stripped my skin. However, this one felt super creamy and gentle and did not burn my skin. I'm not sure how effective it is because I still got acne, but it did not destroy my skin barrier. I probably will rebuy this once I run out to use as a preventative measure. I tend to leave this on my face for 1-2 mins in the shower for full effect.

I've been dealing with hormonal acne for seven months, and nothing seems to work. I've used every acne face wash and serum, I've changed my diet, and I couldn't seem to tame my breakouts right before my period. I'm 40, and I felt like I was in my teens with the way my acne would flare up. This product has cleaned my acne, and I have zero inflammation. The key is to leave the product on your face for 1-2 minutes, and I promise it'll work wonders.

This was recommended to me by my Dermatologist, and I understand why! I have dry, sensitive, acne prone and eczema prone skin. Which is just a LOVELY combination. And this is the only cleanser I've used that moisturizes and cleanses without breaking me out or causing a flare up. I'll be using this until the day I die.

extraits.titre: Great For Sensitive Acne Prone Skin!
extraits.texte: This PanOxyl 4% Acne Creamy Wash has made a noticeable difference in my skin since adding it into my routine. I've seen less redness, fewer active breakouts, and my skin looks a lot calmer and smoother than it did before. I still have some acne marks fading, but the overall texture of my skin has definitely improved. I have pretty sensitive skin, so I was honestly nervous about trying a benzoyl peroxide cleanser because acne products can sometimes leave my skin feeling dry or irritated. This one surprised me because it feels gentle and creamy while still being effective. My skin feels clean after using it, but not stripped or uncomfortable. I also like that the 4% formula feels strong enough to help with breakouts without being too harsh for everyday use. A little goes a long way, and it's been easy to consistently work into my routine. If you struggle with acne but are worried about irritation or dryness, this is one I'd recommend trying!
